headline: How to Maximize Every Inch: A Tiny Home Storage Checklist
articleBody:
- [ ] Assess your belongings — Go through every item you own and categorize it as 'must-have,' 'often used,' or 'seldom used.' This helps you understand your true storage needs.
- [ ] Map out 'dead' spaces — Look for areas like under stairs, above doors, or along unused walls. These are prime candidates for integrated shelving or pull-out units.
- [ ] Consider vertical storage solutions — Think upwards! Floor-to-ceiling shelving, wall-mounted racks, and loft storage can dramatically increase capacity without eating up floor space.
- [ ] Integrate under-floor or platform storage — If your tiny home allows, built-in floor compartments or raised platforms with drawers can be a game-changer for less frequently accessed items.
- [ ] Opt for built-in cabinetry — Custom, built-in storage fits perfectly and seamlessly into your home's structure, avoiding bulky, freestanding furniture that can make a space feel smaller.
- [ ] Designate 'drop zones' — Create specific spots near entrances for keys, mail, and bags. This prevents clutter from spreading to main living areas.
- [ ] Choose dual-purpose furniture — Select items like ottomans with storage, beds with drawers, or benches that open up. Every piece should ideally serve more than one function.
- [ ] Plan for seasonal item rotation — Identify items you only need part of the year, like heavy coats or holiday decorations. Plan a dedicated, perhaps less accessible, spot for them.
- [ ] Create a dedicated pantry or food storage — Even small kitchens can benefit from a well-designed pantry with pull-out shelves or slim vertical storage for groceries.
- [ ] Schedule regular decluttering — A tiny home thrives on intentionality. Regularly evaluate your possessions and let go of what no longer serves you to maintain optimal space.

How to use this checklist: Go through each item and check it off as you plan or implement. This isn't just about adding storage; it's about thoughtful integration and smart design.
